chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the animal slaughtered with plaster and with flint. So he said: There is no valid ritual slaughter except with iron.

key_terms.الذَّبِيحَة: The slaughtered animal; refers to ritual slaughter and its requirements
key_terms.اللِّيطَة: Plaster/limestone; a hard, sharp stone used as a cutting implement
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Flint/chert; a type of sharp stone traditionally used for cutting
key_terms.حَدِيدَة: Iron; specifically an iron implement/blade used for slaughtering
key_terms.ذَكَاة: Tadhkiyah/dhaka — the ritual act of slaughtering an animal to make it permissible for consumption; requires specific conditions

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to slaughter an animal with stone or flint instead of iron in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Muhammad ibn Muslim, one of the closest companions of Imam al-Baqir (AS), asked him about the validity of slaughtering animals using non-iron implements — specifically limestone or calcite (al-liyta) and flint (al-marwa), two types of sharp stones used as cutting tools in the pre-Islamic and early Islamic period. The Imam categorically ruled that ritual slaughter (dhaka) is only valid when performed with iron, establishing a jurisprudential principle that the implement must be iron-based for the meat to be considered halal.

en.hubeali:
تَمَّ كِتَابُ الصَّيْدِ مِنَ الْكَافِي وَ يَتْلُوهُ كِتَابُ الذَّبَائِحِ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ .
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, 
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the (animal) slaughtered by the plaster and by the flint.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no purification except by the iron’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if an animal can be slaughtered with a piece of sharp wood or stone. He (the Imam) said, ‘Without iron it is not a proper slaughtering.”’
